_doc: Velt SDK/component bugs + fixes, keyed by veltVersion. first-shot-css.mjs bakes 'confirmed' css-fix entries into the first-shot stylesheet; the judge pre-checks 'behavior' entries. Only entries whose veltVersion matches the target repo's @veltdev/react are applied.

gotchas.symptom: Send triangle renders pale/greyed. Velt's own .velt-composer--input-button carries opacity:.4 in a state that blends the white glyph into the grey background.

gotchas.component: any injected Velt slot (Composer / ReactionPin / ReactionTool)
gotchas.symptom: 37+ InvalidCharacterError thrown from classList.add when a space-separated className string is put on an injected Velt slot element.
gotchas.fix: Never assign multi-class space-separated strings directly to injected slot elements; apply classes individually or via the wireframe markup you control.

gotchas.symptom: Figma frame exports carry a baked-in N-px margin on all sides (seen 10px on privado composer states), so a frameRegion of {0,0,w,h} includes the margin as content and inflates diffPct.
gotchas.fix: At frame import, compare PNG IHDR dims to the designSpec region; if larger by 2M on each axis, set frameRegion.x/y = M (the margin). Auto-check, don't let the judge re-discover it forensically.

gotchas.symptom: A 2px icon-nudge (margin/translate) overflows a card, which grows a 16px classic scrollbar on Velt's internal .velt-sidebar-content / threads scroller, skewing ALL measured widths by -16px.
gotchas.cssFix: /* clip the nudged icon so it can't overflow: */ .vc-reply-icon { overflow: hidden !important; }
gotchas.fix: When a uniform -16px width regression appears across rows, suspect a transient scrollbar from an overflowing nudge; clip the offending element rather than growing margins.

gotchas.symptom: velt-composer-open is a one-way SDK state with no revert prop — once opened it cannot be programmatically reverted, so a flow that needs the collapsed state after opening can't reach it.
gotchas.fix: Anchor collapsed-state layout/visibility on a STABLE selector, not on toggling velt-composer-open back off (R27). Treat 'return to collapsed' as unreachable and blocker it rather than grinding.

gotchas.symptom: Velt clones wireframe TEMPLATES into the plain DOM carrying the .vc-* classes but DROPS the velt-*-wireframe tag — so a probe/selector keyed to the wireframe tag dies at runtime.
gotchas.fix: Key every runtime selector to a stable velt-* class or your own .vc-* class, never the velt-*-wireframe registry tag (which exists only in the 0-size registry twin).

gotchas.component: measurement harness / any content-bearing surface (comments, notifications, lists)
gotchas.symptom: Whole-surface pixel-diff of a LIVE list against the Figma frame is invalid: the design is DUMMY data (e.g. 2 example comments, made-up names/timestamps) and the app is REAL data (e.g. 11 comments, real text/users). The count/text/avatars/times NEVER match, so pixel-diff either false-FAILs every content-bearing surface (regions everywhere) or gets waved off as 'artifact' — which hides real style defects (the RUN-3 hole: a missing inter-card gap + wrong reaction icons shipped while delta-compare passed on a spec that never checked them).
gotchas.fix: Verify CONTENT-INDEPENDENT style, not screenshots. deltaCompare (per-element computed style + box + inter-card GAP) is the AUTHORITY — it checks the look of ONE card template, identical whether the app shows 2 cards or 200. Whole-surface visualDiff is ADVISORY only: spot a region, then confirm it as a concrete delta assertion (which gates). NEVER flag content (comment count, message text, names, timestamps, reaction counts). The gate rejects a delta spec that covered too little as INCOMPLETE: brief-scaffold auto-derives the inter-card gap + per-slot style elements from the design slice; reaction/action icon identity is icon-lint. A data-controlled single-card capture may set dataMatched to re-enable pixel gating.

gotchas.symptom: @mentions render with Velt's DEFAULT marker/highlighter background (a yellow/tinted block behind the name) because the design's mention style was never asserted into the Connect Map, so first-shot emitted no rule and the default shipped.
gotchas.cssFix:
/* mention: remove Velt's default highlighter bg; the design's own mention COLOR still comes from the Connect Map cssDecls */
.velt-thread-card--message .velt-mention, [class*='velt-mention'] { background: transparent !important; background-color: transparent !important; }

gotchas.symptom: The composer renders as a raw blue-outlined <textarea> with a misaligned @/send, and has no collapsed→active→typing states. TWO causes: (1) the custom CSS never reached the input — the surface is missing shadowDom={false} (or injectCustomCss) so selector CSS can't override Velt's shadow-DOM defaults; (2) the 3 states were never wired — 'active' keys off the .velt-composer-open ancestor class and 'typing' off velt-composer-input-focused, not authored markup.
gotchas.fix: Set shadowDom={false} (or injectCustomCss) on the surface so .velt-composer* selector CSS applies (R6). Build a composer SKELETON (rounded pill container + action row with attach/mention left + circular send right) and wire the 3 states to the real Velt classes: collapsed = default, active = .velt-composer-open ancestor, typing = velt-composer-input-focused. The Judge must DRIVE focus→type and assert all three (a static default capture false-passes the state work).

gotchas.symptom: On-card reactions render as GIANT stacked emoji IMAGES instead of small inline pills with counts — the pin emoji (VeltReactionPin → Emoji/Count) has no width/height and no inline-pill layout, so it paints at the image's natural size. (Also easy to mis-wire the big picker VeltReactionsPanel Item→Emoji in place of the on-card pin.)
gotchas.fix: Lay velt-reaction-pin out as an inline-flex PILL (emoji + count, small gap) and SIZE the pin emoji to the design (velt-reaction-pin-emoji ~16-20px, never natural image size). Distinguish the on-CARD pin (small) from the PICKER panel emoji (larger). brief-scaffold must auto-derive a reaction-pill element so the Judge asserts its box and a giant emoji FAILS as a delta row (the RUN-3 blind spot the KB named but the scaffold never emitted).

gotchas.symptom: TWO identical 'add reaction' (smiley+) buttons render on a comment because BOTH ThreadCard.Reactions AND ThreadCard.ReactionTool were declared. Reactions is the composite row that ALREADY contains the add-reaction trigger; ReactionTool is the STANDALONE add button — declaring both renders the add affordance twice.
gotchas.fix: Use ThreadCard.Reactions (full row: pills + add-reaction tool) OR (ReactionTool + ReactionPin) — never Reactions alongside ReactionTool. lint-customization flags co-declaration of thread-card-reactions AND thread-card-reaction-tool; icon-lint flags two identical reaction-tool glyphs.

gotchas.symptom: The comment dialog renders with NO composer at all. The dialog root was registered as a container wireframe but the Composer subtree was not DECLARED — undeclared children of a container wireframe DISAPPEAR (they do NOT fall back to Velt's default). Easy to miss because an unselected dialog legitimately hides the composer until a pin is selected.
gotchas.fix: Declare the Composer (and Body→Threads→ThreadCard) subtree inside the dialog wireframe. Put Composer in the dialog manifest mustSupply so first-shot + the gate flag its absence. lint-customization's container-completeness check requires declared children when a container root is registered. Judge smoke must drive pin SELECTION and assert the reply composer renders in the dialog.

gotchas.component: any surface on the unstyled base (setUnstyledMode(true,{keepFunctionalStyles:true}))
gotchas.symptom: Own-markup wrappers and slot hosts render with browser defaults (display:block/inline, gap:normal, no flex) — every row STACKS vertically. Measured on a clean build: 28 of ~40 real diffs on the simplest card were pure layout props (display/flex-direction/gap/justify-content/align-items/align-self/padding), and ALL 12 of the builder's appearance-pass fixes were layout reconstruction the plan never carried.
gotchas.fix: The style plan MUST carry the design's layout props for every composing container — the Figma auto-layout frames (brief nodeKind:'layout-frame') hold exactly these decls; map each frame's display/flex-direction/gap/justify/align/padding onto the live container it corresponds to. Layout left unplanned = the builder improvises it per run = inconsistent results.

gotchas.symptom: The SDK renders snippyly-user-avatar as a 32×32 subtree with its visible initial-container anchored TOP-LEFT. Sizing/clipping only the slot HOST to the design's avatar size (overflow:hidden) crops the subtree to its top-left corner — renders as a dark irregular 'blob', not a circle.
gotchas.fix: Size the WHOLE chain to the design's avatar size and center each level: the slot host AND snippyly-user-avatar AND .s-user-avatar-container AND .s-user-avatar-initial-container (width/height/min-width + flex centering). Never clip the 32px subtree into a smaller box. Verified live: all four levels concentric at the design size, letter centered.

gotchas.symptom: The SDK writes the per-user avatar color as an INLINE style attribute (style="background-color: rgb(253,161,146)") on .s-user-avatar-initial-container — a design's avatar fill rule silently loses to it and the SDK's default palette (salmon/etc.) ships.
gotchas.fix: A design-specified avatar fill needs !important to beat the inline style. If the design KEEPS per-user colors, do NOT override — record a defaultOk instead. The value is design-specific; never bake a fixed color globally.
seenOn: harvey (measured live: inline salmon → !important design fill applied)

gotchas.symptom: The avatar initial <span> is EMPTY — the letter lives in its data-modal-author-initial attribute and Velt paints it via CSS content:attr(...). The unstyled base STRIPS that painter, so avatars render with no letter (a correctly-styled empty element, invisible to text checks).
seenOn: harvey (verified live twice: empty span → rendered letter via ::before)

gotchas.symptom: Velt clones a plain BLOCK div (often role=button, e.g. div.velt-comment-dialog-composer) BETWEEN the slot host and your supplied children — flex on the host never reaches the children, so an icon+label or avatar+input+send row STACKS even though the host has display:flex.
gotchas.fix: After flexing the slot host, inspect the live DOM for an intervening clone-wrapper and give IT the row layout too (e.g. `.vc-reply > div { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:<design> }`). The dom-snapshot lists these wrappers — the style plan should carry a disposition for each.
seenOn: harvey (ToggleReply verified live; Composer clone-wrapper verified in the prior build)

gotchas.symptom: A composer host whose internals haven't mounted (unselected card, empty state) collapses to ~18px — the design's ~40px input row renders as a squashed pill.
gotchas.fix: Give the composer host the design row's min-height (design-specific value from the spec node). If the design shows the composer ONLY in a selected state, scope its visibility to the stable selected condition instead of min-heighting every instance.

gotchas.component: own-markup decorative elements (thread connector lines, spacers)
gotchas.symptom: An own-markup decorative <span> (e.g. the thread connector line in the avatar gutter) renders 0×0 inline and is invisible — it has no intrinsic size and the plan carried no box for it.
gotchas.fix: Every decorative own-markup element needs explicit display + width/height + paint, and gutter/connector lines need position:absolute inside a position:relative SDK container (e.g. .velt-thread-card--container) with offsets derived from the design (avatar center column). Hide the trailing instance (:last-child) when the design shows no dangling connector.

gotchas.symptom: replyPlaceholder is a PLAIN STRING — a '{name}' token renders literally in the reply composer placeholder ('Reply to {name}…'), it is never interpolated per-user.
gotchas.fix: Use a static placeholder string, or reproduce per-user text via wireframe tokens (velt-data) in own markup — never pass {tokens} into placeholder props.

gotchas.symptom: Design kebab inside Options.Trigger is invisible (resolve may still show) after a prior patch collapsed .vc-options to 0×0 overflow:hidden to hide the SDK default •••.
gotchas.fix: Never zero the Options host or the mat trigger container when the design glyph lives inside Options.Trigger. Rest-hide via opacity on .vc-options; reveal on card/dialog hover.

gotchas.symptom: Long comment lists are clipped by the host rail with no working scroll — list/content grow with min-height:auto until overflow:hidden ancestors clip them.
gotchas.fix: Scrollport = the list (flex:1 + min-height:0 + overflow:auto). Do not pin the sidebar to a mock frame height (e.g. 832px) that fights the host rail.

gotchas.symptom: Body-level ToggleReply stays display:none on every thread because a CSS :has() keyed on composer NOT having inline style display:none — composer is always mounted and only hidden via a CSS class.
gotchas.fix: Hide Reply only under .velt-comment-dialog--selected / .selected. Never gate on :has(.vc-reply-composer:not([style*="display: none"])).

gotchas.symptom: A wireframe Composer.ActionButton supplied WITHOUT its required `type` prop throws Angular NG0950 (required input has no value) on every render tick — measured live at ~260 errors/sec across all blocks, disrupting cold renders, polluting measurements, and growing the dev log to 1.2 GB before anything looked at the console.
gotchas.fix: Always pass the required `type` prop on Composer.ActionButton in the wireframe markup — type="submit" for the send button (other roles per guide/reference/wireframe-components.md). The structure builder includes it in first-shot markup; console-health.mjs (run right after build-structure) catches the storm mechanically if it ever slips through.
seenOn: harvey (cursor cloud run 2026-07-28, Judge DEFECT-1: NG0950 ~260/s, 1.2 GB dev log; fixed type="submit" → re-verified 0 occurrences/session)

gotchas.symptom: A primitive from the SDK tag registry renders nothing and throws nothing. If it is the R2 context anchor, the entire subtree is silently dead.
gotchas.fix: 8 of 441 registry tags are never passed to defineCustomElement (velt-comment-dialog-body/-header/-options/-priority/-private-banner/-status, velt-comment-sidebar-v2, snippyly-comment-pin). Six are container-shaped names — exactly what a planner reaches for to wrap and anchor. Verify registration with customElements.get() before emitting; manifest/velt-primitives.json now carries registered:true|false.

gotchas.symptom: A React import fails or a whole family looks like it has no React wrapper.
gotchas.fix: PascalCasing the tag is wrong whenever a token moves: velt-comment-sidebar-header-v2 exports as VeltCommentSidebarV2Header, not VeltCommentSidebarHeaderV2. 55 of 441 names were wrong this way. Resolve names against the installed package exports, never derive them.

gotchas.symptom: A behavioural probe reports a working control as dead — the natural response is to "fix" code that is already correct.
gotchas.fix: Velt Angular handlers ignore element.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent/PointerEvent). Verified: a synthetic click on Show-N-replies changed nothing; a real OS click expanded the thread 170->173 cards. Drive behavioural probes through CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent or Playwright locator.click() at freshly-measured coordinates.
